utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we start, just an update on -- without going into any details, but an update on medical reporting. Mr. Jordash, I take it that you have received the answers sent by Dr. Eekhof, which were -- you haven't received them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, we haven't. Whether we have been sent them and we've missed them, I'm not sure. I'll just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was filed, Mr. Jordash. It was filed confidentially, and again I have no intention of going into the details. That's one. And then we received the most recent weekly report from Dr. Eekhof, but that was only very -- one hour ago, two hours ago, I do not know exactly. Conclusions are not any different from earlier conclusions but especially the last weekly report gives more details about certain matters. Is there any reason to specifically deal with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If Your Honour indicates that the conclusions are the same, then -- then obviously we don't raise any point in relation to that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The conclusions are the same. That's -- I'm not saying that all of the content is -- there are new elements in it, but as far as I can see, not worrying. Rather, the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there is one other matter I'd like to deal with before the witness enters the courtroom. That is -- no. One other matter is that we are still working on scheduling of a housekeeping session. What seems to be an option at this moment would be next week, Friday, afternoon. And I am aware that that's perhaps not the -- certainly it's not for the Chamber the most preferred option. If we can deal with some of the matters in time gained during one of our two sessions next week, we might even consider to -- to establish that there is no need for a housekeeping session anymore, which, perhaps, would be preferred above having a housekeeping session of half an hour or 45 minutes and then everyone having to come back or stay in The Hague for that Friday afternoon. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to take a minute of your time to thank the Trial Chamber for their understanding, for the position in which Mr. Petrovic and I find ourselves, and your willingness to move the Status Conference to a later date at the expense of the Trial Chamber's comfort, in the terms of that this session is going to be held on, in other words, on Friday afternoon. Thank you very much, once again, for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. The last matter we briefly have to address is the following: Mr. Groome has asked an opportunity to address the Chamber in relation to exhibits to be used during cross-examination of Mr. Lazarevic, and I will give a brief opportunity to him to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. 27 of the 54 documents the Simatovic Defence intends to use with this witness concern what appears to be a pending criminal case. The jurisprudence of this Tribunal is clear that even absent the criminal conviction, a party may cross-examine a witness on prior bad acts as long as there are reasonable grounds for doing so. This principle was first articulated by the Krajisnik Chamber in its decision on the cross-examination of Milorad Davidovic, dated the 15 December, 2005, and recently followed by the Perisic Chamber in a written decision of the 12th of June, 2009. Both the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the European Convention on Human Rights afford all of us in the courtroom with a right to counsel under Articles 14 and 6, respectively. And while there is no explicit right against self-incrimination in deference to different legal systems, the jurisprudence of the European Court of Human Rights has consistently interpreted Article 6's right to a fair trial to afford an implicit right against self-incrimination. Rule 90(E) of our own Rules reflect the value this institution places on protecting the right against self-incrimination. And while 90(E) empowers the Trial Chamber to compel answers to incriminatory questions as well as give assurances to a witness that such answers will not be used against him, it is not the role of the Prosecution to insulate witnesses from legitimate Prosecutions if these charges are proper and currently pending before the courts of Serbia. Mr. Lazarevic must address them. But the fact that a person comes to this Court to testify does not dispossess them of their rights. And while it may be fair and proper for Mr. Bakrac to ask the witness questions about these allegations, it is must be done in a manner which safe-guards the rights of the witness. The Perisic Chamber recognised in its decision at paragraph 21 that the mechanism afforded in 90(E) for protecting the rights of a witness may not have legal affect before a domestic Court. It adopted a pragmatic approach suggesting that private session could be used to the same effect. It also suggested that a witness may seek the assistance of counsel should the witness deem that necessary before answering certain questions put before him. I would, therefore, make this in limine motion seeking the following relief: One, that both Defence teams be prohibited from asking questions that implicate Mr. Lazarevic's rights against self-incrimination and counsel in open session without a prior discussion with the Chamber. And, two, that if and when such a moment arises, that the Chamber explicitly inform Mr. Lazarevic of his right to request private session and his right to seek the advice of counsel before answering any question in relation to the allegations related to a pending criminal case. And, finally, Your Honours, I will be addressing the issue of the general admissibility of these documents should they be tendered. Ms. Marcus will handle all other objections with respect to this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Any need to respond at this moment? Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will be very brief. The proceedings that have been instituted in Serbia against this person are public, so there is no secrecy involved in this respect. The proceedings -- the investigative part of the proceedings is complete. The -- an indictment has been issued. And a warrant -- a warrant of arrest has been issued as well for this individual. So I would not be opposed if you so decide to discuss these matters in closed session, but, as my colleague said himself, and I believe I understood his words correctly, the right to a fair trial also implies the right of me as one of the Defence counsel of one of the accused to point out to the Trial Chamber any issues relating to the credibility of this witness, especially so as some of his answers in the Milosevic case are -- or tie in with what I am going to question him about regarding certain documents that I obtained from the first lower court in Belgrade in -- through regular channels. These documents were obtained from the first lower court in Belgrade from proceedings that were completely public. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that -- and there seems to be some misunderstanding between you and Mr. Groome, the issue apparently is that Mr. Groome wants to avoid that any questions will be put to the witness which may have an effect on his right to remain silent in his own proceedings, in public, because if we would ask him these questions in public and if the Chamber would use its power under Rule 90(E) to tell the witness that he has to answer the question in view of the still unsettled matter of the effect of any order of this Chamber that a statement could not be used against that person, what the effect would be in any domestic system, that the right not to incriminate himself, which is a right under Serbian law as well, because it directly derives from Article 6 of European Court on Human Rights to which Serbia is a party, that we would -- we would have public statements on matters on which the person involved, a witness before this Court, an accused in Serbia, would be entitled to remain silent on. Therefore, the matter of publicity is not the matter of the public character of the trial, either before this Court or before the court in Serbia, but eliciting from a witness something he could have remained silent upon in a Serbian court would then be part of the public records of this Court, where the protection provided to such a person that it will not be used against him is, at this moment at least, not firmly established, that is, the effect of any such order on domestic proceedings. That seems to be, if I well understood your problem, Mr. Groome, is that -- if it is so, please tell me; if it is not, please correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is a correct characterisation of my argument, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, did you understand what the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I believe I understood you correctly the first time around. But I was probably insufficiently clear. In other words, I have no problems with putting any questions to him in closed session and in him choosing to defend himself by silence or not to answer my questions. As far as I'm concerned, I will put the questions to him in closed session if the Trial Chamber so decides and he may choose not to answer any of my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I indicate our position, although I will not be putting these issues to the witness. Our position would that the only aspect of the witness's -- of the question and answer session that should be in private would be any answers which are compelled. As for the questions, they should be in public, in our respectful submission. As for the warning to the witness about self-incrimination, that should be in public. And if the witness chooses to give up his right to self-incrimination, then the answers should then be given in public. Those are our -- that's our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which leaves open the question of advice to be given to the witness apparently accused in Serbia on whether or not to use his right not to incriminate himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter is clear. Let's get started. The Chamber will carefully listen to any question and as soon, Mr. Bakrac, you enter an area which is related to any ongoing proceedings against this witness before a Serbian court, I would like you to clearly indicate that so as to give the Chamber an opportunity to explain to the witness his rights. And then we'll see whether -- how the witness responds to that. Then the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we continue, in order for the Chamber to appropriately deal with the matter, is a copy of the indictment brought against the witness, is that available? Because if you want to use your right against self-incrimination, it is very useful to know what you're indicted for. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, we have it in the system as well. But our Case Manager is, as we speak, preparing copies of the indictment for -- hard copies for -- for the witness. But it is in the e-court system, both the indictment and its translation. And that is exhibit number, from our list - bear with me, Your Honours - that's 2D8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We we'll ask Madam Registrar to print out copies of the English version of the indictment, not as evidence, but to assist the Chamber in finding its right path in this matter. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it assists the Chamber, I have a copy of the indictment. The only mark on it is the date is circled. So if that assists, then there is no objection from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we would need three anyhow. And since the printer of Madam Registrar is usually functioning well, even without markings of the OTP, I would expect to receive it within two minutes anyhow. So, therefore, thank you for the offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The other thing I have in court, Your Honour, is a copy of Article 6 of the European Commission of Human Rights, if the Chamber should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want us to recite it by heart, we'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm just offering it if it assists the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Jordash will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And a last request, you know what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware. Yes, I am aware. I will try my best and I keep saying that and -- Good afternoon, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was there a time in the RSK when Babic and Martic were disputing elections?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When was that time, please, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very, very -- I can't really give you an approximate time. I wasn't involved in any local politics. I know there was a conflict between them, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you give us a year?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only guess. 1993 or something like that. Or later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's refrain from guessing and speculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was there a time when Babic lost his position in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was replaced by Mr. Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What position did he have before being replaced?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know when he was replaced?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can only guess. I really don't know. I can't remember, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if it was the same time as the disputed -- or the -- when Babic and Martic were disputing the elections?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably would be close to the same time, yes. That was the result of the dispute in the end that one was replaced with the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: At what time do you say you first met Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the day of declaration of RSK becoming a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was the -- what was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the -- after the -- I won't call it a meeting, but a session of the parliament. There was a joint dinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When did you, if any -- if at any time, when did you meet him again or see him again?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never met him, in the sense that we're in the same room where I was introduced to him or this is who I am and things like that. No. I was more aware of him being there through discussion with other people than I would actually see him myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you met him -- sorry, you were at the same joint dinner in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When, if at any time, did you next see him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly the earliest I could remember would be by the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In vicinity of -- between Topusko and Vojnic, that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Visiting somebody, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you find out what he was doing? Did anyone tell you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Pajic mentioned that he was there. That's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic ...

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toso Pajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did he mention the specifics of what Mr. Stanisic was doing at --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- that location?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you meet him or see him after that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only heard of him being there, but not seeing him, no. Physically, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So the two times have you seen Mr. Stanisic during 1991 to 1995 was these two occasions?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones that I do remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And on each occasion, you were not informed of the specifics of what he was present to do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not of the specifics. However, I did get some details about it, but not -- this is exactly what happened. It is more like hearsay, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, what are the details which you heard --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one was the -- one occasion was that he was delivering a message to Babic from -- from Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what were you told was the message?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message that I was told that he came in and delivered the very short message. That's it. You know, You got to pull out from the position that you're in, from the Presidency. And it was told to me like in a joking way kind of -- manner. All he had to do is come in and tell him, You're gone; you're history.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People around Toso Pajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Djuro Skaljac was there. Toso Pajic was there. My understanding was that it wasn't a formal meeting, that I was getting specifics about a meetings or anything like that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. It was -- someone told you in a joking kind of way?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I remember being -- said something about -- I don't know how much history of the Balkans, you know, but there's a terminology called "cvjilan gajter [phoen]." In olden times in the South the wanted to get rid of somebody he would send him a message and the message was a piece of silver rope. How do you do it when I tell you, or you hang yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was the sum total of what you were told?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just about, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably a few other things, but I don't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I had no reason to remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that you never attended any meeting between Toso Pajic and Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You cannot, can you, say with certainty that they did meet in the relevant period, between 1991 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had been told by Mr. Pajic himself that he has to meet him or he met him yesterday or something along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How many times do you think Mr. Pajic told you he had met Mr. Stanisic during the period --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I won't even try to guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did Mr. Pajic tell you, if anything, about what Mr. Stanisic had met him to do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing. It was not a subject of any of our meetings, what Mr. Stanisic does or doesn't do, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So despite seeing Mr. Pajic five times a week, you never learned or understood the nature of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily my job was to do with the army and the UN, not with the police. As far as I was concerned, the police business was the police business.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did anyone else tell you that they'd seen Mr. Stanisic meeting Mr. Pajic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I heard from the other officers at the HQ that Mr. Stanisic was visiting the area, but not who he is visiting or what they were discussing, nothing of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I mean, you have a bunch of officers in the morning during their coffee and a cigarette and the people are talking amongst themselves, you overhear, or you might ask a question, or -- that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did they ever explain to you the nature of the meetings supposed to have taken place between Stanisic and Pajic, or Stanisic and anyone --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- in the locality?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm trying to stress that my interaction with Mr. Pajic had nothing to do with what the police is doing or what the army is doing; it was more on a personal level. So I didn't go to Mr. Pajic and ask him, Oh did you have a meeting with Mr. Stanisic, what did you guys talk about? It was never like that. Neither did he ever offer to me any details about a meeting that he might or might not have. I know they happened, but what is beyond -- behind that meeting, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And yesterday you claimed that Mr. Pajic referred to Mr. Stanisic as Daddy?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Not directly to him on the phone. But when the conversation was over and he put the phone down, he said, That was daddy on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How many times did that happen?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you're asking for something that I can't really give you an answer. I heard it. How often I heard it? I don't know. I heard it. Same as I heard him calling Milosevic Boss. And if you ask me how many times, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest that that evidence you've given is simply not true, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you can suggest whatever you want, I'm standing behind what I said, and I firmly believe this is how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, you have given evidence previously about attending international conferences when Hadzic was President of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that you attended the conferences as a liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was on the list of the delegates I was stated as a liaison officer. Or at least I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did you attend as?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they put me down as interpreter at least on two of those occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But you suggest that you were there as some type of -- surveillance agent?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For a specific person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the conferences you say you went to in that capacity were in June of 1993, in Geneva?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I was in Geneva, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: July of 1993 in Geneva?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 20 to 22nd of July 1993 in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And later in 1993 in Norway?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is supposed to be a kind of secret meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you claim that you would attend -- or the delegates attending that conference from the RSK, including yourself, would attend for briefings in Belgrade beforehand?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who would the briefings be given by?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political side. Every delegation that went to those meetings was split into three groups. There was a political side, civilian side, there was a military side. Two groups, yes. Civilian and military.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you attended the briefings yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was on receiving end after the briefing was completed, because whoever person from the delegation that went to the briefing came back and reported to us. We were all staying in Hotel Mladost in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, can you recall now who gave the briefing for the first meeting, the 16th of June, 1993, Geneva conference?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The 6th of July, 1993, Geneva conference?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's only one person, his face is coming up to me, he's in uniform, he's a Colonel. Can't place the name. At least twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The 20 to 22nd of July, 1993, Vienna conference?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The late 1993 Norway conference, who gave the briefing for that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- I remember specific tasks that I was given for Norway because it was kind of strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What task were you given for Norway?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To stay as close as possible to Admiral Rakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But you don't know who gave that instruction?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that came from Zimonja.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That came from Zimonja?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was not from the briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who gave the briefing for that conference --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- from Belgrade? Don't know. You claim that after the conference -- sorry let me deal with during the conferences. That instructions would come from Belgrade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a need to call Belgrade during the meetings, yes, they would call Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how do you know this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we're in the same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who's in the same room? Let's deal with --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's try and deal with specifics. 16th of June 1993, Geneva?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On all occasions, every meetings that we had, during the adjournments of the meeting all delegation would be brought their own quarters, if you like. Our own had a little room with the telephones. And I remember distinctly that we were told that they were secure lines, meaning that we could call Belgrade and talk whatever we wanted to talk about. It's not going to be overheard by, I don't know, a third party. That was my understanding any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's deal with that. So who would reassure the RSK delegation that the phones were secure?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a man who always represent himself as a host, and he was a Serbian. And he was Milosevic also, but he wasn't Slobo, I mean, it was a different name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the RSK officials accepted, without question, that the lines in Vienna, Geneva, and Norway were secure, and went and took instructions from Belgrade? Is that the evidence you're giving?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Have you to form that question a little bit different. First, it is not instructions. It was more of a, What we do next, and something being suggested from the other side how to continue the meeting. Because if we are taking a break in our meetings, that was -- with some reason it came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But somebody not connected to the RSK delegation would suggest that the phone lines were secure, and the RSK delegation would accept that --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- without question.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And phone up Belgrade to receive instructions in order to make sure that no meaningful agreements were reached in these international conferences. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how big was the delegation on each occasion, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was getting bigger every time we went. First time was a very limited number of people. Not any more than ten, really. And don't ask me, please, who attended because I can't remember all the names. There was list of people who attended it. I'm pretty sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And your position at these meeting was what, as an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the official, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. And nobody in that delegation knew you were working for KOS?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And those on the -- who attended these meetings were the likes of Hadzic and other RSK top officials. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: These international conferences, it was the likes of Hadzic, senior RSK officials, who were attending?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you were attending as an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. And it was physically impossible because the said delegation was clinging to the two groups. The military side of delegation, we discussed problems of military nature with the military part of the delegation by the Croatians. And the civilian part of the delegation, we discussed political issues with the civilian part of the Croatian delegation. So there's no way I could be attending both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. But why were you left in the room when these phone calls these high-powered phone calls for example between Hadzic and Milosevic or Milosevic's colleagues, why from you left in the room?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me ask you a different question. As a part of the delegation, why would they ask me to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Because you were an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I was officially part of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you mind making breaks, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you were attending in some other capacity other than as an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, what was your role?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Get as much information as I possible can on the military side that might interest KOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who gave you that role?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Zimonja.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And he was, as you told us yesterday, the only person who was aware that you worked for KOS?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart probably from the people that served from Belgrade every now and then, please mail some things or ask me some favours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you were in this room with the likes of Hadzic and Zimonja?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zimonja wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So it's you and other -- you and high officials from --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All officials [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- the RSK. And they all thought you were there as an interpreter because they were not aware of your role within KOS --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I believe that they thought about me being a liaison officer for Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So they thought you were there in the capacity as a liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me to guess what they think? I can't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you were there in an international conference with the president of the RSK. Did the president not understand why you were there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea whether he was -- needed to understand when asked the question. I was -- let me try to clarify this, make it more simple, if I can. There is a delegation and all the people are assigned what they are doing there, right? So he is a minister for energy; this guy is either this or that. Now the only thing I could become a party of the delegation would be as something.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they decided I'm going to be as an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the fact of the matter is I have never been used as an interpreter during the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just pause you there then. So everyone knew you were not an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me pause you there as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Everyone at that -- those delegations whether Dusan Rakic, the minister of defence, or Hadzic was aware that were not interpreting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So, presumably, they had some understanding of why you remained in the delegation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again it would be unacceptable to take a part of the delegation and set them out of the room because somebody wants to talk to somebody else. That's what you think? No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No -- they -- they -- Rakic, Hadzic, and so on, were unaware that you were a member of KOS; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So what did they think you were doing in the room?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. Why don't you ask them?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What were they thinking? How can I possibly even guess what they're thinking?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you sat in the room, you didn't have discussions with them, which would indicate your role, and, as far as you're concerned, you don't know what they thought you were doing there.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all seniors to me in every respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can leave it there. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. And could I suggest to you that at no stage did you witness any telephone calls to Mr. Stanisic during these delegations.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never even said that I was present while the members of delegations were talking to Stanisic. I said they were talking to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you're confident that you never heard any of the delegation call up Mr. Stanisic during these international conferences?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean like I'm sitting there, somebody is picking up the phone and saying, Hey, Mr. Stanisic, how are you? I'm calling you from Norway. That kind of call?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, a call to tell him what was going on, to receive instructions, debriefing, whatever.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Debriefing, definitely not. It wasn't done in Norway.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So the evidence you gave in the Milosevic trial, 12411 -- 12410, I beg your pardon, that, on one occasion, Jovica Stanisic was contacted and you said on being -- you believed that on being in the room when those calls were placed - and that's line 16 to line 20 - was nothing less than a lie, was it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your question right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, in the Milosevic trial when asked: "Do you know if, on this occasion," referring to the Norway trip, "Jovica Stanisic was contacted by anyone?" You answered: "I believe that is the case. "Q. And you believe that based on what. "A. On being in the room when those calls were placed."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, which is --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right -- okay. As I said, there were different members of delegation there. And each had a specific task to perform during the meetings. And it always depends who's making the call. Do I make sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Not to me. Perhaps it's me. Please try again.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the actual page could be shown to the witness so that he could see the whole context of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't mean to take advantage, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think you should --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I give you a lot of credit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think you should have a look at the page.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we call up, please, 12410 of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is admitted under seal. Nevertheless, if it is a page which is public on the Internet and not part of the private session, there should be no major objection against it even being shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It is in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't get anything from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps -- actually, the page should be 12410. And perhaps just so the witness gets some context, we can go back to 12409. And this isn't the page, I don't think. No, it's not the page. Can we go to 12409, please. That is the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If can you start reading, Mr. Lazarevic, at line 16.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just read that page and --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole page, from 1 to 16?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: From 16 to the bottom, and then go to 12410. Please indicate when you have finished 12409.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Waiting for the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. 12410, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness sees the same as I do, he can't have read until the bottom of the page because it doesn't appear on the screen. So let's -- Mr. Lazarevic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I give you a couple of extra lines to read, 16 until the end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Next, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You suggested in the Milosevic trial, although you didn't give any details, that a call had been made to Stanisic -- Mr. Stanisic during the Norway trip. But ten minutes ago you told the court definitely not. So I'm just trying to clarify --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it wasn't or it was made? Which one are you trying to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, that is a matter for you to clarify, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I believe that is the case. Doesn't say that I definitely state that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. If that's your answer, we can move on. Thank you. Let me take you to the final subject I'd like to deal with, which is the issue of Pauk. Were you aware, Mr. Witness, of a declaration signed --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a second. This is a very annoying habit you have: Either you call me Mr. Lazarevic or call me Mr. Witness all the way through, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes, I do not see the real problem. Sometimes Mr. Jordash addresses you as Mr. Witness or sometimes he may address you as Mr. Lazarevic. I do not see any inappropriateness in not always addressing you exactly in the same way. I can imagine myself doing it as well, as a matter of fact, without any bad intentions. Therefore, Mr. Jordash, you may proceed. And if you wish to meet what is apparently experienced as unpleasant by the witness, you may choose to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I shall. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, let me deal with Pauk. Were you aware of a declaration signed by --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you aware of a declaration signed by Fikret Abdic in Belgrade with Radovan Karadzic in the presence of Slobodan Milosevic in late 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try to see if you might remember something to do with it. That the declaration was a 12-point declaration recognising the autonomous region of western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you this then: Have you -- did you hear, in the summer of 1994, of approximately 80.000 refugees fleeing from Bosnia into the RSK, into the region of Topusko, Muslims, refugees?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Velika Kladusa, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I know it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. At the time of Pauk, the Operation Pauk, there was around 8.000 [sic] Muslim refugees who were camping out in the RSK, hoping to return home at some point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, they came to no man's land between the Serbian side and Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Fikret Abdic was trying to return to the western Bosnia and take the refugees back with him.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You have no idea about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Oh, I know about the presence of the refugees, if that's what you're asking me. But I don't know about Fikret Abdic going and pleading with them to come back. That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you aware that the refugees wanted to return home?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't spoken to any of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I -- you had finished your last answer when you said "No, I haven't spoken to any of them" when I interrupted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please put your next question, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The 21st Corps and the 39th Corps and the 15th Corps were fighting within the Pauk Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Wasn't one of the purposes that they were trying to achieve was the return of Fikret Abdic to western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the real reasons for it. I did find it rather strange that the Serbs were fighting the Muslims for the Muslims. That I did find strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So it's your evidence, and then if you really don't know, then I'll leave it for the Court to decide, but you really don't have any evidence to give about the refugees and their intentions during 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1994 and end 1995? I know of one instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm talking about November 1994 until Operation Storm. Was there an effort by the corps I have just mentioned to protect the refugees?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very end, yes, I am aware of that. But their all pulling out of western Bosnia, if that's what you're suggesting. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the only other time that I knew about the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me then move to a slightly different subject. Petrova Gora, where the Serbian MUP camped out, was a high-tech facility, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was led to believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it was high-tech because it had high-powered surveillance equipment, listening devices, to enable the MUP to listen in to various electronic communications.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always thought it was merely to do with the telephone connections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They can click into somebody's conversation to listen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. It was this -- the particular location where the Serbian MUP was was primarily a surveillance location, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When the Serbian MUP was there.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they used it for, but they used it as a HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was it on a mountain?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really a mountainous region. Let's say it was on a high hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. A high hill with high-tech listening devices?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was how many kilometres away from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, not even a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that location where the Serbian MUP camped out was a different location to the rest of Pauk, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just repeat the question slowly this time, because I'm trying to distinguish whether you asked me whether there were two commands or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The formations that you have told the Court were taking part in Pauk, including the Serbian MUP, as you would have it, were divided in locations. The Serbian MUP at Petrova Gora, and the rest of the Pauk Command within Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including Serbian MUP in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was in Bosnia? Who had their HQ in Bosnia from the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I was going to get to that. So Bozovic had his HQ in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kladusa itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah. Legija had HQ --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know whether he was a member of the MUP Serbia or who he was a member of, but he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Legija who you're not sure was a member of MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was that he was a member of this special unit that came from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Positively? Yes, I know he was a member of MUP. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Because you just said that you're not sure.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nowadays, I can't be sure of anything, the way you are asking me the questions. So if I go back and think, yes, Ulemek was in charge of special unit by the MUP Serbia police, had their own camping grounds somewhere, I don't know, Vojvodina, somewhere else, I don't know. There. And his involvement later on in happenings in Serbia suggested that he is a member of MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat last sentence? And his what later on? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Involvement in things that happened in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Later on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Such as?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Such as? What happened later on that suggested his involvement in Pauk?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Haven't you followed these trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I know from a newspaper. He was involved in the killing of President Djindjic and some other people there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So basically, from what you've just said to us, you didn't know that he was a member of the MUP, but due to events which occurred later as, for example the killing of President Djindjic, you then put two and two together and --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I knew he was a member of MUP. I couldn't just allocate him; I couldn't put him in a set or specific role there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How did you know he was a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the insignia, they are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The insignia on the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was Frenki Simatovic based at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was led to believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was his HQ?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Bozovic and Legija had an HQ with who?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: With who?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Pauk.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who was there in Pauk?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In charge was General Novakovic, Mile.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You had a Chief of Staff who was Colonel Bulat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the people that I met. And what they told me is the HQ of the Pauk, which was about 200 yards as you get across, it was in a simple house. That's where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Further down the road when you go into Kladusa, you come to -- I don't know how to translate it, Robna Kuca. It's like supermarket. And on the first floor there was an office where Mr. Bozovic had his HQ. I'd say "operativni brod."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Operational area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Bozovic and Legija were based in this HQ you've just told us about and they had men with them in that HQ?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who was with Frenki Simatovic in Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never got to get in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So you don't actually have any evidence concerning Frenki Simatovic or Bozovic and their relation to each other, or do you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I what?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you have any evidence concerning their relationship --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you consider evidence? I don't quite follow what you're trying me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap because of the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, that's my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's both your faults.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It won't happen again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, it will.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Not from me it won't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You saw Mr. Bozovic two or three times a month at the HQ of the 21st Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You never saw him at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never been to Petrova Gora when they took over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. You never saw Simatovic, Mr. Simatovic giving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sorry. Just take a breath after every answer. I have seen situations where other members of the team would play some of the role which I would be forced to play if you continue this way. That is to either kick you or to pull your legs or whatever, pull your arms. I'm really relying on the inventivity of the team as a whole. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You didn't see Mr. Simatovic giving orders to either Mr. Bozovic or Legija, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In person? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. Thank you. The men that you say belonged to Arkan, did you ever see Arkan give orders to them at Pauk?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You never saw Mr. Stanisic giving orders to Mr. Simatovic at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you never saw Mr. Simatovic reporting to Mr. Stanisic at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The men you identified as belonging to Arkan were clearly separate to the men that you suggest belonged to the Serbian MUP. They were a different formation, were they not?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that. All I know they were on the same ground fighting the same -- fighting on the same side. But if you're suggesting that Arkan came there by himself, I doubt very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that you couldn't identify the difference between the men you say belonged to Arkan and the men you say belonged to the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course you can tell the difference. I think the other guys had a little tiger head on their shoulders.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The only place you saw the men who were with Mr. Simatovic on a regular basis was Petrova Gora, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I keep saying that I never went to Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask to you turn to your previous statement again. Perhaps this is the quickest way to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please, could we have on the screen the witness's 1999 statement, 0205-3036.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's -- before I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we just make sure it's not being broadcast. Excuse me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I beg your pardon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Before, Mr. Witness, we turn to that statement, could you please describe the insignia you say that Arkan's Men were wearing in a little more detail?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember it correctly, they had a tiger's head with open jaws.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What colour was the tiger?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orange.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the uniform? Was there a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me the things that happened, like, 15 years ago of people I met maybe twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was it a uniform --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was the uniform worn by Arkan's Men the same as the uniform worn by the Serbian -- the men you say were part of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way: They were not the JNA uniforms. They looked to me like a NATO uniform. And if you ask whether there was any colour distinction between the uniform, no, there was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Page 25 of the English version, please, and the paragraph I'm looking for in the B/C/S starts with: "Altogether, Arkan had about 100 men at Petrova Gora ..." Can we turn to that in the B/C/S, please. Can I be helped out?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's -- it should be around the page 20 -- thank you, page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Witness, find the: "Altogether Arkan had about 100 men at Petrova Gora ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not on the B/C/S version. It's a different page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Page 23. Thank you, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, these are matters which should be well prepared. It's not that difficult. I even can do it. So would you please take care next time that we're not loosing time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see that paragraph, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he had around 100 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I'm looking for the line about four lines down: "Arkan's troops all wore the same uniform with -- but with no obvious rank insignia."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecution that at the time, that they had no rank insignia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably did. I don't remember. This is a minor detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go further down to the next paragraph where it says: "I never saw any of Stamatovic getting supplies so I don't know if they were supplied from elsewhere or if the Arkanovici also collected their supplies as well." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. But I'm listening to you, basically the truth, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, have a look at the paragraph, please. Do you see that -- sorry. Do you see where it says: "In fact the only place I ever saw the special police with regularity in the RSK was at Petrova Gora."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is that what you told the Prosecution at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this Petrova Gora -- basically this sentence does not necessarily mean a location. It means the area. It's the same name. If I saw you in Petrova Gora doesn't mean I see you at the HQ in Petrova Gora. I saw you in Petrova Gora. It's a large national park. And then have you have your own security perimeter around the HQ, which I never entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. But that national park, again, was different to the HQ in Bosnia of the remainder at Pauk, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Part of it was in Bosnia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No. The appointment I'm making is that seeing Stamatovic's men in the park at Petrova Gora was different -- a different location to the HQ Pauk in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, different location, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you never saw Mr. Simatovic's men socialise with Arkan's, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, in fact, they had a strained relationship, as you saw it, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was just my judgement. I -- you have to understand, I did not spend days on days just watching what they are doing on location. I hardly ever saw them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In the short time that you were able to observe the two groups, you observed they had a strained relationship, because Arkan's Men had a reputation of being thieves and murders.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the general opinion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was your opinion, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a general opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was that your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably mine. I still think that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And in contrast to that, Stamatovic's police unit at Petrova Gora regarded themselves as upright policemen?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have never been at Petrova Gora HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It was your view that they regarded themselves --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the special police from Serbia I thought to be absolutely correct in their behaviour and demeanour, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Their behaviour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I might add: In all that time, the only problem that I did have was with the members of Arkan's unit and not with the members of the Mr. Simatovic's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the -- Simatovic's men viewed Arkan's Men as common criminals. That was the view --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was it's view you reached, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was the view you reached, from what you observed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite -- I'm trying to see what you said. Oh I reached ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you reach that view?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know what is the relationship between two different units on the ground. All I can vouch is to what the general opinion is about Arkan's men and what I have find out in my dealings with the MUP Serbia or with the Arkan men. And the problems that did I have with the Arkan's men not with the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to point out that counsel puts a lot of questions that ask the witness to express what other people thought and what other people believed. And don't think the witness is in a position, necessarily, to know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, although he seems not to have a hesitation to tell us what the general opinion was, et cetera. So, therefore, it's not without a reason, perhaps, that Mr. Jordash elicits this. I am, at the same time, Mr. Jordash, I'm looking at the clock. Usually we have a break after 75 minutes. We are beyond that. And since you indicated yesterday that you would need an hour, I thought you might want to finish that hour in the next three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can finish now. That's the end of my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Jordash. We'll first have a break. But before taking that break, I would already ask Madam Usher to escort Mr. Lazarevic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An issue was raised about putting questions to the witness about a case which apparently is pending against him in Serbia. What exactly, in what kind of detail would you like to go, and in order to establish what, Mr. Bakrac, so that we have a better view on the matter? I heard that there were many documents related to this, if I well understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. And I do not intend to use all of those documents, as I've already told my learned friend, Mr. Groome. In our country, there -- proceedings have a concern structure. First the police conducts an investigation. Then submits a criminal report. Then a prosecutor would submit a request for proceedings. And then -- to the investigating judge, and then the investigating judge, once he has completed his investigation, would forward it to the prosecutor who would then issue an indictment. So this criminal file is rather large, and I just wanted to pick certain documents from each part in this whole procedure and present it to the witness. The decision on his arrest, an APB that was issued, and a brief description on his involvement in fraud, whereby he defrauded some 45 individuals and two companies in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what do you intend to establish through this?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I am trying to assist the Trial Chamber in assessing the credibility of this witness and his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For purposes of procedure, you have provided the Chamber with a copy of the -- copy of the indictment. I, meanwhile, was able to read that. What is there else -- apart from asking the witness can either say, Of course, that's what I did. First of all, I would like to find out whether he is aware of the proceedings. I do not know if there's any knowledge among the parties whether he is aware of being indicted in 2006 for this matter. That's -- Then I -- to put to the witness, what could he say? I mean, the mere fact that a court apparently based on the testimony of witnesses considers there's sufficient reason to indict him is at least a relevant element, that he may not be the honest citizen you would expect a citizen to be. But to go into any further details, where we get stuck is that this Chamber cannot form an opinion on any such matter, apart from assuming that, if there's evidence, if there's detailed information about who are the parties who apparently have paid him, reading in this, that it should seriously keep in mind that Mr. Lazarevic may well be culpable of such fraud, which would then, of course, have to be considered. But to go in any further detail, I wonder what the Chamber could do with that. We can't try Mr. Lazarevic here. We don't have the evidence before us. What we have before us is that the Court considered the evidence sufficient to indict Mr. Lazarevic which is a clear signal that it's not just a loose allegation, as it was in the decision underlying the -- as it was in the factual situation underlying the decision in the Krajisnik Chamber. That it was, of course, quite a bit different from what we find in Perisic, in relation to Mr. Sacirbey. But what else do you want to establish? I mean, this Chamber is not assisted by going to go a bit of here and get a bit of there of that case.
